title: Backward And Forward Induction Can Conflict
body_html:
Backward And Forward Induction Can Conflict

MFoGT Figure 6.21 adds an initial stage before the battle-of-the-sexes game with outside option. The continuation subgame has the forward-induction outcome $(T,L)$ with payoff $(3,1)$.

Backward induction then says player 2 should stop at the first stage and obtain payoff $2$. But if player 2 continues, forward-induction reasoning interprets the continuation as evidence that player 2 expects more than $2$, which changes the beliefs used in the later subgame.

This illustrates why forward-induction refinements are usually applied only when the rationality interpretation is coherent.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 6.7 and Figure 6.21] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. Example where backward-induction and forward-induction reasoning are incompatible.
